newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea gold demand up on weak dollar, low price.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea gold demand up on weak dollar, low price.

text.p: South Korean gold demand picked up this week due to falling prices on the domestic market and the won's strength against the dollar, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Domestic gold demand is reviving from the end of last week, aided by recently falling prices in world market and strengthening won against the dollar," a trader with Tong Yang Global Corp said.
He said the won rose in line with the yen's strength versus the dollar in world market.

Daily selling price for the precious metal by South Korean gold producer LG Metals fell on Tuesday to 10,200 won per a gram from 10,360 won a week ago. The price is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market.
The company's silver price also fell back to 150 won a gram from 154 won a week earlier.
But some traders said the nation's sluggish economy hit by corporate financial woes would limit the rising gold demand.
"We have no choice but to cut some of our bullion businesses on concerns about possible payment defaults by our clients," a trader with a major bullion house said.

Traders said the domestic silver market showed signs of a slight supply shortage as major trading companies, suffering from huge foreign exchange translation losses early this year, were seen cutting imports.

Meanwhile, the Korea Exchange Bank quoted on Tuesday the telegraphic transfer dollar selling rate for customers at 894.80 won, slightly down from 894.10 won a week ago. The rate is regarded as the benchmark won/dollar rate for companies.
